text:
alex: FYI quick flag - after the kernel-selector reorder that landed yesterday I see a throughput wobble on long-seq requests (6k-8k). Small batches (1-4) dip 12-18% on p50/p95. attaching a short flame and stats.

marta: can you drop the perf numbers and the exact commit?

alex: commit: 5b3c9f2 (selector: prefer low-latency kernel when batch_size<=4). Quick numbers from perf harness on a8g:
```
seq=8000 bs=1  -> before:  21 tok/s  after: 18.3 tok/s  (-12.9%)
seq=8000 bs=4  -> before:  78 tok/s  after: 64.1 tok/s  (-17.9%)
seq=512  bs=8  -> before: 450 tok/s  after: 462 tok/s  (+2.6%)
```
flame: main cost step moved from matmul->fused-attn launch overhead (~320us extra on average) when selector picks "fast-init" kernel for short batches.

ravi: sounds like launch overhead dominates when small batch + long seq. Did we accidentally bias toward kernels with higher startup but better steady-state?

jen: also watch KV cache warmup: when requests are sparse we see cold KV cache misses that prolong the first few tokens, which interacts badly with kernels that rely on large fusion setup. if the selector doesn't account for avg_prefix_len the wrong kernel gets picked.

alex: exactly. current selector is just heuristics on batch_size and seq_len threshold; it doesn't consider prefix reuse or historical KV hit rate. I instrumented a few traces: if kv_hit_rate<0.7 and seq>4k we should favor lower-launch kernels even if they have slightly worse per-token flops.

perf-bot: regression-alert: test perf/inference/long_seq_kernels failing on canary. id=canary-2026-03-14-1794 link: https://ci.internal/reports/1794 (summary attached) :warning:

marta: can we quantify launch vs throughput tradeoff into a single cost model? like cost = launch + token_time * seq. then pick kernel with min expected cost given batch_size and kv_hit_rate estimate.

ravi: +1. ran a quick sweep with a toy cost model locally:
```
kernel A: launch=320us, tok=0.00012s/token
kernel B: launch=80us,  tok=0.00014s/token
for seq=8000, bs=1 -> costA = 0.00032 + 8000*0.00012 = 0.96032s
                      costB = 0.00008 + 8000*0.00014 = 1.12008s
so A wins for long steady runs, but if kv_hit_rate < 0.15 (meaning repeated cold starts), effective seq reduces -> B can win.
```

jen: KV effective seq idea is good: effective_seq = seq * kv_hit_rate + warmup_penalty*(1-kv_hit_rate). we can measure kv_hit_rate online per token via the tracer.

alex: implemented a micro-autotuner that runs short probes when route sees a new seq/batch profile. probe chooses both kernel A and B, measures 300 tokens each and estimates launch+tok. results:
- probe latency overhead ~ 1-2ms per route, acceptable for canary
- autotuner switched to kernel B for interactive low-kv routes and kernel A for high-throughput backfills

marta: nice. did you run this under continuous batching? continuous batching changes the apparent batch_size distribution. we need the selector to consider scheduled batch composition probability, not just instantaneous bs.

ravi: good call. continuous batching introduces a launch amortization across requests that come in within the same scheduling window. I modeled P(coalesced)=0.35 for our 5ms window; effective_batch = bs + P*mean_inflight. that can flip the kernel choice.

alex: we added scheduling-awareness: selector queries scheduler_estimator(route) which returns expected_coalesced_bs. After enabling that, the perf regression disappears in my local rig. numbers: seq=8k nominal bs=1, with coalesce=3 -> costA becomes better.

perf-bot: perf/regression-alert cleared for local-canary-1794.

jen: can we A/B this? plan: rollout autotuner as opt-in canary (5% of traffic on dedicated pools), collect kv_hit_rate, coalescing rate, and real-world token throughput. if stable for 48h -> promote. also add a fallback to previous selector on >5% error spike.

alex: created PR with config and metrics: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rt/merge/2198. includes metric names: rt.selector.chosen, rt.selector.cost_estimate, rt.selector.probe_latency, rt.kv.hit_rate.

marta: add an integration perf test that simulates sparse interactive traffic (poisson arrivals) + long prefixes so we don't miss this again.

ravi: also add a guard: if kernel_init_time variance > 2x over 1min, prefer stable low-launch kernel for that route. we've seen jitter on certain hw (older cuda drivers).

alex: writing up a short postmortem and action items. TL;DR: reorder changed bias, launch overhead + KV-cold + continuous batching interactions caused regression. Fix: cost-model + scheduler-aware autotune + canary rollout.

jen: thanks. :thumbsup:

marta: assign to runtime-ops to monitor for 72h after rollout.

alex: will do. rolling patch to canary now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
